primitives.name: One-Epoch Screening
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Baseline: random search over HP configs; evaluate each at minimum fidelity (1 epoch); select top-K=3; train only those to maximum fidelity (100 epochs).
primitives.assumptions: Early-ranking assumption: correlation between 1-epoch loss and full-training loss.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Poor scaling with high noise, non-stationary fidelity gaps.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Conformal prediction with early-stop bandits. GSE: Rapid, low-fidelity model evaluation (e.g., few-season gradient boosting) to filter candidates before expensive full-validation.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between early-stop metrics (e.g., AUC on first batch) and holdout performance.

primitives.name: Top-K Tournament
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Baseline: random search over HP configs; evaluate each at minimum fidelity (1 epoch); select top-K=3; train only those to maximum fidelity (100 epochs).
primitives.assumptions: Selection bias correction under finite samples.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Over-selection leads to exploitation of noise.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Knockoff-filtered variable selection. GSE: State-based filtering (e.g., 'hot stock' detection) followed by detailed analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of true winners among selected candidates.

primitives.name: Learning-Curve Ranking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Assumption: early-epoch ranking is informative of final ranking — validated empirically via learning-curve visualizations (1,000 sampled curves colored by final rank; rank-evolution heatmaps).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-monotonic or multimodal fidelity gaps destroy ordering.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Transfer learning across fidelity distributions. GSE: Time-series state transitions (e.g., player form decay modeled via curve fitting).
layer2.telemetry: Spearman correlation between early and late rank orders.

primitives.name: Compute-Tradeoff Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Numerical results / baselines - Final test RMSE of 1-Epoch ≈ 100-Epochs policy (curves converge to the same point), but 1-Epoch uses 40× fewer training epochs (500 vs 20,000).
primitives.assumptions: Diminishing returns in fidelity improvement relative to computational cost.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Flat reward landscape makes cheap approximations sufficient.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Adaptive experimental budgets via sequential hypothesis testing. GSE: Resource-constrained optimization (e.g., budget allocation across predictive models).
layer2.telemetry: Marginal gain in accuracy per additional epoch of computation.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that multi-fidelity HPO (MF-HPO) aims to reduce compute by evaluating cheaper approximations of model performance. However, the authors show that a simple "1-epoch screen" followed by a full-train tournament (Top-K) often matches the performance of sophisticated MF-HPO methods while using orders of magnitude less compute. This is because the early learning curves exhibit a "dominant subspace" phenomenon: good hyperparameters quickly align with optimal parameters, stabilizing early losses, while poor ones remain noisy. The key operator is a threshold-based filter (1-epoch loss < τ) that projects onto this dominant subspace. In GSE, this maps to rapid, low-fidelity model evaluation (e.g., few-season gradient boosting) to identify promising candidates before committing to full validation. The failure mode occurs when fidelity gaps are non-stationary or when early rankings are destroyed by noise, requiring adaptive thresholds.
